# Owner's Manual

## Remote Software Upgrade

The vehicle receives software upgrades without a visit to the service center. An upgrade is downloaded while driving and installed later. To install the upgrade the vehicle must be parked on a level surface and remain parked for the whole installation. The installation takes about twenty minutes. During this time the vehicle cannot be driven and must not be unlocked. Lights and sounds signal the installation: the instrument cluster stays dark, the hazard warning lights may flash briefly, and a chime sounds when the vehicle is ready to be driven again. If the installation is interrupted, the vehicle keeps the previous software and the upgrade is offered again after the next trip.

## Media at a glance

The media menu groups the radio, the connected phone, and the stored music. Sounds from any source can be adjusted in the sound settings: balance, fader, bass, treble, and the equalizer presets. Speed-dependent volume raises the sounds from the speakers as the vehicle gets faster and lowers them again when it slows down. The sounds of the car's own warnings, such as the seat belt reminder, are not affected by the media volume and remain audible at their set level. Press and hold the volume knob to mute all media sounds at once.

## Driving tips

### Things to remember when driving

#### Exhaust gas particulate filter

The exhaust gas particulate filter collects soot from the exhaust. It regenerates by itself while driving: the soot is burned off at high exhaust temperatures, which takes a few minutes of steady driving and needs no action from the driver. Regeneration can continue briefly once the engine is switched off. Audible noise, such as from the radiator fan, several minutes after the engine is shut off is normal. Do not switch the engine off during a drive to interrupt regeneration. Frequent short trips can prevent the filter from regenerating fully; in that case take a longer drive on an open road.

#### Driving with a trailer

Adjust the speed to the load and the road. Brake early and gently on a descent, and select a lower gear so that the engine braking supports the brakes. Check the tire pressure of the trailer before each trip.
